memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "After a long time Judah's wife, the daughter of Shua, died. When Judah had recovered from his grief, he went up to Timnah, to the men who were shearing his sheep, and his friend Hirah the Adullamite went with him. When Tamar was told, 'Your father-in-law is on his way to Timnah to shear his sheep,' she took off her widow's clothes, covered herself with a veil to disguise herself, and then sat down at the entrance to Enaim, which is on the road to Timnah. For she saw that, though Shelah had now grown up, she had not been given to him as his wife." - Gen 38:12-14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Time passes. Judah's wife dies, and after his mourning he goes off to shear his sheep. Meanwhile, Tamar has realized the bitter truth: Shelah is now grown, yet she has still not been given to him. Judah has broken his word. She has been wronged and forgotten, left with no future in a world where a childless widow had little security.

So Tamar forms a desperate plan. She disguises herself and positions herself on the road where Judah will pass. We should be honest: the means she chooses are not something the Bible holds up as a model to imitate. Yet the passage also helps us understand her. Here is a woman who has been deeply wronged, denied what was rightfully hers, and pushed into a corner by a man who should have protected her. Out of that desperation, she acts.

The Bible does not paint Tamar as simply wicked, nor Judah as simply innocent. It shows us a tangled, painful situation where a powerless person, failed by those responsible for her, takes a risky and morally complicated step to secure the justice she was owed.

This should stir compassion in us for those pushed to desperation by injustice, and caution in us about the wrongs we might do to the vulnerable. God sees the whole story — both the sin and the suffering — and He is a God who ultimately brings justice and works even through tangled situations.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I have compassion for those driven to desperation by injustice?
2. How might my failures push vulnerable people into hard corners?
3. Can I trust God to bring justice even in tangled situations?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me compassion for those wronged and pushed to desperation. Keep me from being the cause of another's corner, and help me to trust You to bring justice and to work through even tangled stories. Amen.
